brief.headline: Pre-Market Briefing: Nifty Eyes Open as US Tech Surges & BPCL Greenlights ₹1.3L Cr Project
brief.summary: Indian equity markets face a defensive start following global tech-led rallies and local corporate catalysts. BPCL approved a massive ₹1.27 trillion refinery complex, while public sector banks reported record first-half profits. Global markets look to strong US performance led by heavy tech gains.

takeaways.text: BPCL approved a ₹1,26,656 crore integrated greenfield refinery and petrochemical complex in Andhra Pradesh.
Public sector banks posted a 17% rise in H1 net profit, touching an aggregate ₹1.09 lakh crore by September 30, 2026.
KEC International secured new orders worth ₹1,407 crore across transmission and distribution segments in India and Africa.
Blackstone sold a 1.55% stake in International Gemological Institute via block deals for ₹280 crore at ₹417 per share.
US markets closed higher with Nasdaq jumping 2.31% and S&P 500 rising 1.60% as tech shares rebounded strongly.
OpenAI accused Apple of pressuring suppliers to shun its devices amid escalating trade-secret disputes.

sections.india: Indian equities enter the session after the Nifty 50 closed down 1.07% at 25607.2 and Sensex fell 1.17% to 83339.26. Key stock triggers include BPCL's approval of a ₹1.27 trillion refinery complex in Andhra Pradesh, KEC International's ₹1,407 crore new order wins, and robust H1 public sector bank profits crossing ₹1.09 lakh crore. Meanwhile, SEBI is exploring a specialized platform to regulate the pre-IPO grey market, and jewellery counters remain in focus amid strong YTD gains.
sections.world: Global markets closed on a strong note overnight, with the S&P 500 surging 1.60% and the Nasdaq climbing 2.31%. Brent crude dropped 3.98% to $90.84, offering relief to oil-importing economies like India, while gold rallied 3.75% to $3668.5. In credit ratings news, S&P cut France's outlook to negative while upgrading South Africa's credit rating, pushing it closer to investment grade.
sections.tech: In the technology sector, OpenAI accused Apple of pressuring device suppliers to shun its products, widening their trade-secrets dispute. Elon Musk noted that Alphabet's Google is interested in renting additional compute capacity from SpaceX. Concurrently, Nasscom warned that AI could shrink traditional IT maintenance and call center markets while creating new avenues for Indian technology providers.
